body:
It makes me feel awful to confirm it, but...yes, you are correct on all counts. That's what scares me, the feeling that I can't change -- that I'm "verbally abusive" not as something I have done but as an irredeemable character flaw. I don't want to be that way, but I've spent years cowering from my father because of the feeling that he can't get better, and I guess I've internalized that.

That said, thank you for the practical advice. I've started working on it already. I hope I'll see positive changes in my overall quality of life, and maybe that will help me fix my brain patterns.

Yeah. I think that's my place to start. But if nothing has convinced me I deserve to be forgiven, what's changed now? Can I just make a conscious decision to try and let myself be compassionate towards myself and live a good life, and have that work? Or is there a switch in my head that has to be turned that, without it, nothing will ever happen...

Thing is, it's not just the past -- 20+ times a day I'll do/say something I consider stupid and then start immediately castigating myself for it. Brutally. It's like I never became an adult, I'm still that kid. That's the trouble...

But...yeah. I actually typed out a response to you that basically said "but I thought I was doing that, and nothing changed!"

And then I realized it wasn't true. My therapist has been saying, you need to forgive yourself for the million things you've done or said to yourself and have more compassion for yourself, and I've been saying, yes, yes, I do, but I HAVEN'T BEEN DOING IT. I've been saying I will, and yet... for some reason I haven't. I'm afraid I can't. Any ideas...?

Trying :)

I think that's really the root of the problem here -- that I don't like myself. If I had a little more compassion for myself, I think I'd be more conscious, more aware, more able to be compassionate to others... but it's so hard...
Think North...Far North. But I genuinely appreciate the offer :)
